text:
Carla S: Heads up — noticed a CI run that ended up applying a cluster-scoped RBAC change against the gpu-training namespace. Looks like `deploy-sa` was bound to a cluster role. Log snippet: `PATCH /apis/rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1/clusterrolebindings/ci-deploy` with user `ci-runner@infra`. Is anyone seeing this too?

Dave P: Can you paste the exact binding yaml? ideally `kubectl get clusterrolebinding ci-deploy -o yaml` if it still exists. Also which pipeline job created it?

Carla S: Pasted the output from the control plane logs (sanitized):
```
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: ClusterRoleBinding
metadata:
  name: ci-deploy
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: ClusterRole
  name: cluster-admin
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount
  name: deploy-sa
  namespace: ci
```
The pipeline job `ci/deploy:release` shows the `kubectl apply -f rbac.yaml` step run by `ci-runner`.

sec-bot: Security Alert — clusterrolebinding creation detected (high privilege) by principal `ci-runner@infra` at 2026-02-05T14:02:31Z. Audit ID: sec-8f3b.

Bob L: Oof. That binding gives namespace-scoped SA cluster wide rights. Quick mitigation options: 1) delete the ClusterRoleBinding and create an equivalent RoleBinding scoped to `gpu-training` namespace, 2) restrict the pipeline to only use ns-scoped manifests, or 3) add a Gate in CI to prevent `ClusterRoleBinding` resources in application repos.

Alice M: We should also assume keys/tokens might be misused. Rotate the KMS-wrapped tokens for `ci/deploy` credentials (we store the wrapped blob in Secret Manager). Check KMS decrypt logs to see if the wrapped blob was decrypted outside normal run times.

Dave P: I'm running an audit query now: `kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector involvedObject.kind=ClusterRoleBinding --since=24h` and also pulling API server audit logs for `ci-runner` entries. Will post findings shortly.

Carla S: Quick plan I'm proposing:
- remove `ci-deploy` ClusterRoleBinding (temporary)
- create `deploy-ns-gpu` Role + RoleBinding in `gpu-training` granting only the required verbs on pods/deployments/secrets (least-priv)
- add CI guardrail that rejects cluster-scoped RBAC manifests from app repos
- rotate CI deploy credentials (KMS) and check decrypt audit
I can own the RBAC edit and the CI guardrail patch. ETA 2 hours if nobody objects.

Bob L: Sounds good. One caution: removing the ClusterRoleBinding may break in-flight canary deploys for other services that relied on it. oncall-ops, can you watch the deploy dashboard while we do the change?

oncall-ops: Will monitor. Please post the exact deletion command before you run it so I can halt if needed.

Carla S: Deletion command I'll use: `kubectl delete clusterrolebinding ci-deploy --context=prod` then create Role and RoleBinding: `kubectl apply -f ns-deploy-role.yaml -n gpu-training`. I'll open a short maintenance window for the change.

Dave P: Audit notes: I see the `ClusterRoleBinding` was created by the pipeline image `release:v2` at 14:02:31Z. There's a single `aws:kms:Decrypt` event in the same minute by `ci-deploy-key` and IP matches our known runner pool. No extra decrypts outside that run for the last 30 days.

Alice M: Ok rotate KMS keys anyway (schedule a rewrap, short TTL on new tokens). I'll kick off key rotation and post new wrapped secret.

Bob L: I'll add a quick CI lint that runs `kubeval` + a small JS rule to block `kind: ClusterRoleBinding` and `kind: ClusterRole` in non-infra repos. PR coming in ~30m.

Carla S: Thanks — I'll proceed in 10m. Posting final checklist: pre-checks (audit snapshot, note current binding), run delete/create, smoke test deploy to gpu-training, monitor logs + oncall. Will update thread when live. :white_check_mark:

sec-bot: Note attached — incident ticket created: SEC-2026-032. Severity: medium (privilege exposure, no sign of lateral misuse).

Carla S: Done — clusterrolebinding removed and namespace RoleBinding applied. Smoke deploy succeeded. No failed jobs observed in the 15m window.

oncall-ops: Observed one short-lived failed deploy for `edge-proxy` (requeue), recovered automatically. No pager.

Dave P: I'll keep the audit watch for another 48h and add an automated query to alert on any future clusterrolebinding creations by CI service accounts.

Alice M: KMS rotation in progress, will post completed when done.

Bob L: CI guardrail PR merged to `main` -> will block new clusterscoped RBAC manifests and fail builds with `forbidden: cluster-scoped RBAC`.

Carla S: Closing out here. Folks assigned: Carla (RBAC fix & docs), Bob (CI guardrail), Dave (audit watch), Alice (KMS rotation). Follow-ups: write runbook for this class of issue and add to oncall playbook. Thanks all. :pray:
